title: Mittens' Lost Bell
markdown:
Gertie the goblin had a ball, a super bouncy fuzzy moss ball, boing boing, and right beside her Mittens the cat purred like a little engine. Mittens was sleek and black. On her collar a tiny shiny bell went ding-dong, ding-dong when she wiggled, like happy raindrops.

Sunbeams danced on the napping rock, warm golden ribbons. A peaceful afternoon. Then Mittens sat up, green eyes like emeralds wide. She shook her head, flick-flick, shake-shake. No happy ding-dong. The special bell was gone.

“Oh nooo,” Gertie squeaked, eyebrows nearly at her hat. Mittens nudged the empty collar. A sad mrrrow. Whiskers drooped. Gertie did not name the feeling. She shook her own head instead. “Don’t you worry. We’ll find it. We always do. The glowworm glade this morning. Maybe it fell off there.”

Hand-in-paw they went, grass sighing secrets to the breeze. The glade was not spooky. Glowworms blinked like teeny fairy lights, warm pools on the leaves, a sparkly dream. They tiptoed. Mittens looked under a mushroom bigger than Gertie’s head. Gertie peeked behind dewdrops. No bell. No ding-dong.

“Where else did we play?” Mittens remembered the high rocks where Gribble the ogre lived, gentlest biggest giant, famous for wobbly puddings and bubbly soups.

A smell arrived: warm, berry-sweet, a little like giggling sugar. Gribble stood by a huge jiggly pudding that quivered like happy jelly, apron almost clean except a smudge of purple berry juice on his round friendly nose, stirring with a spoon as big as Gertie.

“Hello, Gribble!” Mittens offered a hopeful mrrrow.

Eyes crinkled. Voice like warm thunder. “Gertie! Mittens! What brings you to my wobbly pudding world?”

“Mittens lost her special bell. The one that goes ding-dong. We think it fell when we were playing near here.”

He set the giant spoon down with a soft thump. “That simply won’t do.” He looked at his big feet, around him. “I was sweeping spilled snowberry dust and flour. Things get jumbled when I’m making wobbly puddings. Perhaps…”

He rummaged a smooth bowl of fluffy white flour. Clink-clank-ding-dong. The silver bell, a little flour on it, perfectly fine, shining.

Mittens squeaked. Tail dancing. She nudged the bell. Gertie giggled with relief. Gribble beamed, winked, and did not turn the find into a lecture on carefulness, only admitted that even careful cooks get jumbled, especially with wobbly puddings around. He fastened the bell to the collar.

Ding-dong.

Mittens purred, rubbing a flour-dusted leg. They waved and headed home, the little bell singing as Mittens trotted. The sun dipped, pinks and oranges. Safe, and jingling.

And so Gertie and Mittens learned that a lost treasure, even a tiny one, can turn up where pudding and flour have been having a jumble, if you keep looking with a friend and ask the cook who smelled like berries. The sweetest surprises hide in the most delightfully wobbly places, and they come home ding-dong, ding-dong, like raindrops that found their way back to the collar.
